verdict.rationale: mise documents plugins as a backend type, can still use asdf plugins, and lets users point a tool at a third-party vfox plugin repository through the MISE_BACKENDS_<TOOL> override. The evidence shows how to consume and select existing plugins and backends, but not how a developer authors and publishes a new one, so coverage of extending the manager is incomplete. Missing for 10: documentation on authoring custom plugins or backends (plugin API/SDK), third-party tap or overlay registration, and independent hands-on corroboration of third-party plugin extension.

support.subject: As a developer, I can extend the manager through third-party taps, overlays, plugins, or backends

citations.quote: A backend is where mise installs a tool from: a package registry such as npm or cargo, a release host such as GitHub, or a plugin.
mise is compatible with asdf `.tool-versions` files and can still use asdf plugins when needed.
You can override the backend for any tool using environment variables with the pattern `MISE_BACKENDS_<TOOL>`
